So how do you glue two cities together? Not easily. When the river froze,
even the bridge of boats was useless. The nearest real bridge? Vienna, 250 kilometers away.
The story goes, in 1820, Count Seccini reached this river on his way to his father's funeral.
The ice wouldn't let him cross. He waited about a week and missed it, so he pushed for a permanent
bridge. Two British engineers built it, both named Clark, not related. In 1849, the chain bridge
opened. And on it, even nobles had to pay the toll. I have to pay to walk? The cities grew together.
